assumptions.statement: V_l is finite with no uniform upper bound, and X_l is the finite product of standard-Borel coordinate spaces.
rho_l is a probability law, m_l=exp(-H_l)rho_l has finite strictly positive mass, and pi_l is its normalization.
K_l is normalized, positive, measurable, and parameter independent; rho_l K_l and m_l K_l define the next measure pair.
A fixed jointly measurable reverse-kernel version Pi_l(dx|z) disintegrates pi_l(dx)K_l(x,dz).
The nonlinear action chart is an open L-infinity ball; every required exponential and derivative is uniformly bounded there.

At every admitted scale the interaction tier has finite standard-Borel product structure, a declared product probability nu_l equivalent to pi_l, and every nonempty subset interaction in hierarchical zero-mean gauge. Admission of a scale arrow separately requires pi_l K_l to be equivalent to a declared target product reference. Interaction-degree covariance uses a componentwise/permutation Borel realization or another explicitly proved grading intertwiner.

Each retained interaction space is closed and has a declared bounded idempotent projection with a declared operator norm and quotient residual norm; a gauge-covariant retained theory additionally requires the projection to intertwine the declared gauge realization.
One principal G-bundle induces belief and model statistical bundles; actions, references, kernels, sections, connections, and scale morphisms carry the stated equivariance data.
Statistical paths are differentiable in quadratic mean with centered finite-L2 scores, and parameter-independent pushforwards stay in the selected coarse family.
For the explicit spectral realization, X_i are iid N(0,1), b>=2, Z=b^(-1/2)sum_i X_i, and Hermites use the normalized probabilists' convention.
Ordinary spectra, fixed points, and beta differences use declared bounded scale isomorphisms J_l to one normed reference object.
Generalized mode sections have fixed norm, sign or phase, and per-volume normalization; only tempered scale-gauge changes are admitted as equivalences.
Q_l is a smooth regular configuration manifold with declared Fisher metric and a locally existing unique VFE vector field; the coarse configuration map is separately smooth.

Kernel RN, kernel-KL, disintegration, and randomization claims use standard-Borel targets; every density tier has one fixed family-level sigma-finite reference and finite jointly measurable density versions, fixed sigma-finite integration is localized to finite-measure pieces, fixed-observation formulas use declared measurable RCP versions, and signed integrals obey the stated no-infinity-cancellation condition.

At each selected observation the evidence slice M_o has mass z in (0,infinity) and posterior Pi_o=M_o/z; L_ext=log z-KL(Q||Pi_o) is primary for every probability Q, while the classical expected-log split additionally requires Q<<Pi_o and separate H4 log-integrability.

An operational environment node is a standard-Borel state law plus a normalized measurable message kernel; this types an observation kernel as an interaction without asserting biological autonomy or deleting the conditioning sigma-algebra.

Variational attention is represented by finite normalized categorical source labels with positive priors and finite measurable source energies. On the selected complete-record slice the augmented likelihood is exactly a finite measurable label-free latent factor times the displayed per-label observation factors, no other record or generative factor reads any source label, normalization over the full record space is declared model data, and the constant-row softmax additionally assumes the separate recognition factorization.
Every external theorem or attribution uses a checked primary source or authoritative monograph with an exact statement and hypothesis mapping.

Chapter 12 uses external philosophical positions only as explicitly cited interpretive vocabulary; manuscript-specific idle-wheel, ontological-fit, and operational-holonomy claims remain separately status-tagged and require their own bridge or settlement evidence.
Numerical stability claims use deterministic controls through condition number 10^14, high-precision comparisons, scale-aware error bounds, and machine-readable JUnit output.
Verification binds the complete declared input policy, separates update from nonmutating verify mode, and records source revision, UTC timestamp, and semantic payload digest.
Scale depth l, inference-orbit coordinate r, Fisher duration, and physical time are distinct; a shared fine/coarse history requires a positive oriented semiconjugacy factor.

claims.statement: For every finite standard-Borel agent network of arbitrary finite cardinality, every finite interaction hypergraph on it, and every normalized parameter-independent blocking channel satisfying the declared domination, product-factor, gauge-equivariance, smoothness, and integrability hypotheses, construct a typed scale-indexed measure-pair, action, full-interaction, score-tangent, bundle, configuration, and history theory whose exact coarse maps, derivatives, contractions, defects, generalized modes, cocycles, beta data, fixed objects, pullback compatibilities, extended ELBO identities, and exact-versus-projected boundaries satisfy the obligations atomized in the bound claim ledger.
claims.quantifiers: For every finite vertex set V_l with no upper bound on |V_l|; every finite standard-Borel product space X_l=product_{i in V_l} X_{l,i}; every finite interaction hypergraph; every probability reference rho_l; every finite positive likelihood measure m_l=exp(-H_l)rho_l; every normalized parameter-independent Markov kernel K_l:X_l rightsquigarrow X_{l+1} admitted by the stated hypotheses; every declared principal G-bundle, pair of associated statistical bundles, compatible scale morphism, DQM score path, full Hoeffding interaction, retained projection, regular configuration manifold, and selected fine history meeting its local assumptions; and every finite composable sequence of such scales.
claims.falsifier: An admitted finite typed instance that violates any universal conjunct, or any unresolved load-bearing ancestor, blocks affirmative closure.

claims.statement: The normalized kernel defines rho_{l+1}=rho_l K_l, m_{l+1}=m_l K_l, preserves the finite evidence mass, and defines the extended RN action R_l^H=-log(d m_{l+1}/d rho_{l+1}).
claims.quantifiers: Every scale l and every pair and kernel satisfying H-MEASURE and H-MARKOV.
claims.falsifier: A normalized admitted kernel for which domination, mass preservation, or the Radon-Nikodym action fails under the recorded hypotheses.

claims.statement: Q_l(phi)=-log d((exp(-phi)m_l)K_l)/d(m_l K_l) is defined for every bounded phi and is locally real analytic from the declared open L-infinity ball to L-infinity(pi_{l+1}); where both base actions are finite it equals their difference.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and every phi in the declared open ball under H-REVERSE and H-CHART.
claims.falsifier: An admitted bounded increment for which the conditional log-Laplace map leaves L-infinity or lacks a convergent local derivative expansion.

claims.statement: DQ_l(0)[phi]=E[phi|Z] and D2Q_l(0)[phi,psi]=-Cov(phi,psi|Z) as bounded typed maps on the declared action chart; normalizing the perturbed probability adds the separately displayed centering terms.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and bounded phi,psi under H-REVERSE and H-CHART, as almost-everywhere identities for each fixed input equivalence class.
claims.falsifier: A valid finite kernel whose difference quotient disagrees with the conditional mean or whose second derivative disagrees with minus conditional covariance.

claims.statement: U_l is a contraction from Lp(pi_l) to Lp(pi_{l+1}) for every 1<=p<=infinity, is the unique extension from bounded functions when p is finite, and preserves every defined mean.
claims.quantifiers: Every l, every 1<=p<=infinity, and every phi in Lp(pi_l).
claims.falsifier: A normalized parameter-independent admitted kernel with ||E[phi|Z]||_p>||phi||_p.

claims.statement: ||phi||_2^2-||U_l phi||_2^2=E Var(phi|Z)>=0, with equality exactly for joint-almost-sure coarse-measurable phi; on DQM scores this is the conditional Fisher-information loss.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and phi in L2(pi_l).
claims.falsifier: A square-integrable admitted tangent for which total conditional variance or its equality criterion fails.

claims.statement: The bounded RN action map is globally additively homogeneous and U_l 1=1, so both descend to action quotients by constants while evidence mass remains a separately tracked scalar.
claims.quantifiers: Every l under H-MARKOV and the explicitly projective tier.
claims.falsifier: Two bounded representatives differing by a constant whose coarse RN actions fail to differ by the same constant.

claims.statement: On L-infinity/R1 with oscillation norm, ||overline(U_l)||<=delta_l; a negative accumulated log-delta rate relative to B_{n<-l}->infinity is a sufficient, not necessary, nonautonomous irrelevance certificate, with log0=-infinity.
claims.quantifiers: Every l with the fixed reverse-kernel version and every finite cocycle segment; the asymptotic certificate assumes B_{n<-l} tends to infinity and the displayed limsup is negative.
claims.falsifier: A bounded quotient function exceeding the Dobrushin oscillation bound, or either finite counterexample failing under its stated compatible laws.

claims.statement: For a bounded positive unital operator on the declared complex Banach lattice with quasi-interior unit, all-compacts Calkin convention, and recorded pole/positive-eigenfunctional hypothesis, r(U)>1 implies r(U)=r_ess(U).
claims.quantifiers: Every operator satisfying the full Banach-lattice, Calkin, pole, and positive-dual hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: An operator meeting every hypothesis with r(U)>1 but r(U)>r_ess(U), or a missing strict-positivity step for the dual eigenfunctional.

claims.statement: For the specified Haar circle inverse-branch kernel, Uf=f composed with doubling has r(U)=1 on L-infinity and r(U)=2^alpha on complex periodic C^alpha with the sup-plus-Holder norm for 0<alpha<=1, where alpha=1 is Lipschitz.
claims.quantifiers: Every 0<alpha<=1 for the specified Haar circle kernel; the Holder space is a separate Banach-space witness, not an instance of the Banach-lattice theorem.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the 2^(alpha n) upper bound, the matching fixed-Fourier-mode lower bound, or the inverse-branch reverse-kernel identity.

claims.statement: For every finite interaction network, hierarchical zero-mean extraction P_l and assembly E_l are bounded inverse maps between the full nonempty-subset Hoeffding interaction space and the bounded action quotient; ||E_l||<=1 and ||P_l||<=3^|V_l|-1, with worst-case-sharp finite-size dependence.
claims.quantifiers: Every arbitrary finite V_l under H-INTERACTION, including the declared trivial empty-network convention and with no maximum cardinality.
claims.falsifier: A bounded action class whose power-set extraction fails to reconstruct it modulo constants, a normalized interaction not recovered by extraction, or a product probability whose extraction norm exceeds the proved finite-size bound.

claims.statement: At every admitted interaction scale a declared product reference nu_l is equivalent to pi_l and supplies the hierarchical normalization; this is a per-scale premise rather than an automatic consequence of a Markov arrow. Under the declared grading realization and transformed Markov/RN square, product coordinates, the nonlinear interaction map, and residuals are gauge covariant as equivalence classes.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and every scale arrow and gauge change satisfying H-INTERACTION and H-GAUGE; componentwise/permutation realization is the declared sufficient grading hypothesis, not a uniqueness claim.
claims.falsifier: An admitted scale lacking target product equivalence, a claimed grading-covariant gauge action failing the declared intertwiner, or an RN interaction map that violates the transformed kernel square.

claims.statement: T_l^G=P_{l+1} overline(Q_l) E_l is the exact nonlinear full-interaction coarse map. At every bounded interaction g its typed Frechet derivative is P_{l+1} overline(U_l^{phi_g}) E_l, with fixed U_l only at g=0; along an exact orbit these derivatives form a cocycle between adjacent interaction spaces.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and every bounded g_l in the full finite interaction space under H-INTERACTION.
claims.falsifier: An induced higher-order term missing from the full output, a bounded center where recentering fails, or a derivative whose domain, codomain, or tilted conditional operator disagrees with the displayed chain rule.

claims.statement: The retained update is a bounded idempotent projection of the exact interaction output. Its coordinate residual and quotient residual satisfy P_{l+1} rbar_{l+1}^Q=r_{l+1}^G and rbar_{l+1}^Q=E_{l+1}r_{l+1}^G with the proved two-sided finite-size bounds; they vanish for all retained inputs exactly when the exact image is invariant.
claims.quantifiers: Every declared bounded idempotent retained projection and input under H-PROJECTION, with the empty output treated by the trivial convention.
claims.falsifier: A nonzero omitted residual labeled exact, a claimed invariant retained space with a nonzero residual, or failure of either inverse identity or finite-size norm bound.

claims.statement: The iid product DQM score is E_b h=sum_i h(X_i), the coarse pushed score is L_b h=E[E_b h|Z], and every centered L2 h is realized by the stated squared linear density path.
claims.quantifiers: Every centered h in L2(mu_*) and integer b>=2.
claims.falsifier: A centered L2 h for which the path is not normalized or lacks DQM score h, or whose product/pushforward score differs from the formulas.

claims.statement: At the Gaussian fixed law, L_b e_k=b^(1-k/2)e_k and the centered L2 spectrum is {b^(1-k/2):k>=1} union {0}; k=1 is relevant, k=2 marginal, and k>=3 irrelevant under the fixed norm and block convention.
claims.quantifiers: Every integer b>=2 and normalized probabilists' Hermite index k>=1.
claims.falsifier: A Hermite mode violating the Mehler conditional-expectation identity or incompleteness of the claimed spectral closure.

claims.statement: Cross-scale mode equations are typed as M_l v_{l,a}=lambda_{l,a}v_{l+1,a}, or transported to a reference endomorphism; exponent invariance requires both tempered scalar mode normalization and tempered distortion of the complete comparison trivialization and its inverse.
claims.quantifiers: Every exact interaction orbit, comparison trivialization, and mode section satisfying H-MODE and H-REFERENCE; exponent conclusions only when the limit or stated limsup exists.
claims.falsifier: An ordinary eigen-equation across unequal spaces, or the identity cocycle equipped with superexponentially distorted scale norms that changes the apparent exponent.

claims.statement: Composed exact derivatives and normalized generalized eigenvalues satisfy the ordered cross-scale cocycle law lambda_{n<-l,a}=product_{k=l}^{n-1}lambda_{k,a}; an autonomous semigroup is asserted only after compatible stationary identifications.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite composable scale segment and normalized invariant line.
claims.falsifier: A composable segment for which ordered derivative composition or scalar multiplication fails, or semigroup language without stationary identification.

claims.statement: Nonautonomous scale diagrams use invariant sections in each typed tier; an ordinary fixed point is formed only after the scale maps become endomorphisms of one declared reference object.
claims.quantifiers: Every admitted nonautonomous diagram and every tier named in the statement.
claims.falsifier: A fixed-point subtraction or equality whose operands inhabit distinct spaces without a declared identification.

claims.statement: The discrete interaction beta is [J_{l+1}^{-1}R_l^GJ_l(g)-g]/log b_l; any continuous covariant scale derivative requires a separate smooth scale manifold, Banach bundle, interpolation, and scale connection unrelated to the contextual gauge connection.
claims.quantifiers: Every l with b_l>1 and declared reference isomorphisms; continuous claim only under the stated extension.
claims.falsifier: A beta subtraction between unequal spaces or a continuous derivative without the required smooth bundle data.

claims.statement: The score is S_{l,H}[phi]=-(phi-E_pi phi), an isometric isomorphism from L2/R1 with Fisher norm to L2_0, and S_{l+1,R_lH}[U_l phi]=E[S_{l,H}[phi]|Z].
claims.quantifiers: Every l and phi in L2(pi_l).
claims.falsifier: A representative dependence after quotienting or a failure of the centered conditional-expectation square.

claims.statement: For a smooth parameter-independent normalized Markov fiber morphism Psi_l, Delta_F=g_l^F-(T^V Psi_l)^*g_{l+1}^F is positive semidefinite and equals conditional score covariance.
claims.quantifiers: Every selected DQM fine/coarse family and vertical tangent under H-GAUGE and H-DQM.
claims.falsifier: An admitted parameter-independent fiber map that increases Fisher norm or lacks the stated vertical tangent type.

claims.statement: A cross-scale associated-bundle morphism is globally defined only after the principal map is G-equivariant and the smooth statistical-law fiber map intertwines the represented G-actions; the sample-space kernel and induced law-manifold map remain distinct typed objects.
claims.quantifiers: Every adjacent scale arrow and both belief and model channels.
claims.falsifier: Two representatives of one associated-bundle point that map to different target classes because the fiber intertwining equation fails.

claims.statement: Composable base maps, principal maps, law-fiber maps, and associated-bundle morphisms satisfy their ordered identity and composition laws before the scale family is called a functor or cocycle.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite composable sequence of scale arrows and both associated channels.
claims.falsifier: A pair of admitted adjacent arrows whose composed bundle morphism differs from the declared direct arrow.

claims.statement: The covariant first-jet chain rule retains the vertical horizontal-defect term, its exact composition law, and every signed cross term in the base Fisher comparison; positivity follows only when that defect vanishes.
claims.quantifiers: Every related fine/coarse section and tangent under H-GAUGE.
claims.falsifier: The trivial line-bundle identity map with source horizontal field d/dx and target horizontal field d/dx+a d/dy, for which the uncorrected fine-minus-coarse base tensor is negative.

claims.statement: Related sections and horizontal-lift-compatible bundle morphisms pull the vertical Fisher defect to h_l^omega-f_l^*h_{l+1}^{omega'}>=0; without the commutative first-jet square, the vertical mismatch term is retained.
claims.quantifiers: Every l, base tangent, and related section satisfying H-GAUGE and the compatibility square.
claims.falsifier: A claimed defect pullback when sections are unrelated, horizontal lifts fail to commute, or the omitted mismatch is nonzero.

claims.statement: Each configuration manifold is an explicitly selected finite-dimensional or Banach/Hilbert section manifold, and its strong Fisher metric is either the pullback of a declared joint-law Fisher metric or a labeled weighted product metric with base measure, channel weights, gauge quotient, finiteness, and nondegeneracy data.
claims.quantifiers: Every scale at which a natural-gradient vector field or Fisher duration is asserted.
claims.falsifier: An all-smooth-sections space with no manifold topology, a weak metric with no gradient, or a weighted marginal metric labeled the exact joint Fisher metric without block orthogonality.

claims.statement: The configuration coarse map from Q_l to Q_{l+1} is separately typed, symbolically disambiguated, and smooth; it is not identified with the law, action, interaction, reference-space, or bundle coarse map.
claims.quantifiers: Every l for which a configuration-level history comparison is made.
claims.falsifier: A history theorem using an abstract kernel with no smooth tangent map, or a configuration symbol already assigned to a reference-space endomorphism.

claims.statement: A pointwise bundle morphism induces a configuration coarse map only after the transformed fine section is constant on fibers of the base coarse map and smooth descent is proved, or after a separate smooth gauge-equivariant averaging or variational construction is supplied.
claims.quantifiers: Every admitted fine section when a pointwise-induced configuration map is asserted.
claims.falsifier: The base collapse S1 to a point with identity fiber map and fine section Q(x)=sin x, which cannot descend to a section over the point.

claims.statement: Independently recomputed fine and coarse VFE vector fields share an oriented orbit only if T Rhat_l X_l=a_l(X_{l+1} composed with Rhat_l) with a_l>0; otherwise only a fine path and its pushforward are compared.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and every configuration in the domain under H-CONFIG and H-HISTORY.
claims.falsifier: A shared-history claim with a nonpositive factor, a failed tangent equality, or an independently optimized coarse orbit not related by semiconjugacy.

claims.statement: A nonconstant shared oriented history additionally requires a nonzero pushed vector field on every regular subarc and appropriate maximal-interval conditions; semiconjugacy alone may collapse every fine orbit to a point.
claims.quantifiers: Every fine orbit for which nonconstant or global shared-history language is used.
claims.falsifier: A constant configuration coarse map with a zero coarse vector field, which satisfies the semiconjugacy equation but collapses nonconstant fine orbits.

claims.statement: Under semiconjugacy the exact fine and coarse Fisher speeds are recorded separately; duration equality requires configuration-metric compatibility along the orbit and does not follow from fiberwise Fisher contraction.
claims.quantifiers: Every regular semiconjugate orbit segment with finite configuration Fisher speeds.
claims.falsifier: The identity map and identical vector fields on R with metrics dx^2 and 4 dx^2, for which semiconjugacy holds while coarse duration is twice fine duration.

claims.statement: For every probability Q and every selected positive-finite evidence slice M_o=z Pi_o, the primary ELBO is L_ext=log z-KL(Q||Pi_o), its safe gap identities hold in the extended reals, its relative-log representation has integrable negative part when Q<<M_o, and H4 is required only for the classical split.
claims.quantifiers: Every probability law Q on the declared latent space and every selected slice satisfying H-ELBO.
claims.falsifier: An admitted Q for which log z-KL is undefined, the gap identity requires infinity cancellation, or the relative-log negative part exceeds the proved z/e bound.

claims.statement: For a family mu_t=f_t lambda plus atoms and no singular-continuous part, a common sigma-finite dominator exists exactly when the union of all positive atomic supports is countable; arbitrary singular-continuous components require a separately declared common singular reference.
claims.quantifiers: Every family of mixed Borel probability laws on R of the displayed form.
claims.falsifier: A family with countable positive-atom union not dominated by the displayed common reference, or an uncountable positive-atom union dominated by a sigma-finite measure.

claims.statement: If probability kernels K_x<<L_x have a standard-Borel target, refining partition ratios produce a finite jointly measurable RN version; localization proves fixed sigma-finite integration measurability, and a common-dominator perspective/martingale argument proves kernel-KL measurability without partition cofinality.
claims.quantifiers: Every pair of probability kernels with standard-Borel target and every fixed sigma-finite reference satisfying H-PROBABILITY.
claims.falsifier: A dominated standard-Borel kernel pair for which the finite partition-limit version fails the RN identity or joint measurability, or for which the perspective partition divergences fail to increase to kernel KL.

claims.statement: Every normalized Markov kernel contracts KL for arbitrary input probability laws in [0,infinity]; equality/recovery is inferred only on the finite-KL branch. For a fixed measurable fine RCP o maps to P_o, declaring the coarse version pointwise as P_oK makes the fixed-evidence coarse extended ELBO nondecreasing for arbitrary recognition Q at the same selected evidence representative.
claims.quantifiers: Every pair P,Q of probability laws and normalized measurable parameter-independent Markov kernel K; the pointwise fixed-evidence corollary additionally uses standard-Borel spaces and a declared measurable fine RCP version.
claims.falsifier: An admitted normalized K with KL(PK||QK)>KL(P||Q), a recovery conclusion drawn solely from infinity equals infinity, or failure of the declared pointwise pushed kernel P_oK to disintegrate the pushed joint.

claims.statement: For every nonempty agent block B, a fixed measurable baseline RCP version and its posterior-full regular outside set define an arbitrary-law conditional extended VFE whose zero gap is the exact conditional posterior; singleton B is an agent and general B a meta-agent, while pointwise version invariance is only posterior-outside almost everywhere.
claims.quantifiers: Every nonempty block of every finite standard-Borel interaction network with context-indexed normalized baseline and record kernels, family-level jointly measurable densities, and the H-ELBO slice hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: A regular outside state for which the incident slice fails to normalize or its conditional extended gap differs from conditional KL, or a claim of version-independent exceptional-point values.

claims.statement: For two finite-KL joint laws with the same outside marginal, the collective VFE difference equals the outside expectation of the conditional block-VFE difference; block ascent is therefore ascent of the same collective objective, not automatically of evidence.
claims.quantifiers: Every block pair satisfying the stated common-outside-marginal and finite posterior-KL hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: Two admitted laws with the same outside marginal for which posterior KL disintegration leaves a nonconstant residual in the VFE difference.

claims.statement: The collective VFE contains each actual interaction record once, and a correlated attention-label recognition law adds the conditional total-correlation term omitted by a product-row ledger.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite factor hypergraph and every admitted correlated conditional attention-label law.
claims.falsifier: A normalized factorization in which an actual record must be duplicated in the joint or the conditional TC correction has the opposite sign.

claims.statement: Every normalized standard-Borel observation kernel has an operational environment-node randomization, and every environment-node message marginalizes to an observation kernel; the equivalence preserves rather than deletes the conditioning sigma-algebra.
claims.quantifiers: Every normalized observation kernel on standard-Borel spaces and every normalized environment-node message policy.
claims.falsifier: A standard-Borel normalized kernel with no measurable uniform randomization, or an environment policy whose marginal is not a normalized measurable kernel.

claims.statement: Under the complete label-exclusive augmented likelihood, a categorical latent source label with positive prior and finite source energy yields the exact posterior attention row; under the separate constant-row recognition factorization its VFE is KL(beta||pi)+tau^{-1}sum beta E[D] and has the stated softmax minimizer.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite source set satisfying the full selected-record factorization, full-record normalization, integrability, and recognition conditions in H-ATTENTION-LABEL.
claims.falsifier: A model satisfying complete label exclusivity for which Bayes' formula or the Lagrange multiplier optimum differs, or a correlated-label law with no TC correction.

claims.statement: R_i^x is defined at first use with its source, target, and passive frame-change direction, and every later gauge formula uses the same convention.
claims.quantifiers: Every channel x, agent i, overlap, and gauge change in the revised source.
claims.falsifier: A three-frame composition or transformed density using the reciprocal convention without an explicit change of variables.

claims.statement: The measure-level pushforward law is general; the determinant density formula is asserted only for the Lebesgue or declared relatively invariant reference tier.
